Set coordinates:
\[
A=(0,0),\quad B=(1,0),\quad C=(1,1),\quad E=(0,1)
\]
so \(AB=BC=EA=1\), with \(\angle A=\angle B=90^\circ\).

Since \(CD=DE=1\), \(D\) is the intersection of unit circles centered at \(C=(1,1)\) and \(E=(0,1)\). Convexity gives
\[
D=\left(\frac12,1+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right).
\]

At \(E\), the vectors to adjacent vertices are
\[
\overrightarrow{ED}=\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right),\qquad \overrightarrow{EA}=(0,-1).
\]
Thus
\[
\cos \angle E
=
\frac{\overrightarrow{ED}\cdot \overrightarrow{EA}}{|ED||EA|}
=
\frac{-\sqrt3/2}{1}
=
-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
So
\[
\angle E = 150^\circ.
\]

\[
\boxed{150}
\]
